\noindent{\large\textbf{S2 Table. All contrasts of the pre-specified trader comparison, both windows.}}

\smallskip
\noindent Kendall $\tau_b$ of score $a$ and score $b$ with each later trader label, their difference $\Delta\tau=\tau(a)-\tau(b)$, and percentile intervals from one paired wallet bootstrap per label (2,000 resamples, seed 42; the same resample indices for every score). The plan (S1 File) fixed every row of this table before the rows were computed, but not before every input was known: in W1 the coefficients of the two counts, AWP and the C-PR walks on all six labels, and of both EndorseRank variants on the liquidation-free close rate, had already been computed with 400 resamples, so the W1 point estimates of P on every label and of Q on that rate were implied, and EndorseRank $-$ AWP on that rate had itself been computed. No W0 association with a trader label had been computed. Only P and Q on the liquidation-free close rate in W1 enter a decision, judged on the 97.5\% interval (Bonferroni level of that pair); all other intervals, including every 97.5\% interval outside that pair, are unadjusted and descriptive. Stratified rows average $\tau_b$ within strata of 3--4, 5--9, 10--24 and 25 or more label-window closes, weighted by the number of wallet pairs. $^{\dagger}$Label grows with the number of closes. $^{\ddagger}$Walks over raw-amount allowance and transfer layers and their mixture at $\lambda=0.5$, which belong to a companion study (Kwon et al., manuscript submitted to \emph{IEEE Access}); they are listed here because the plan included them, and the main text does not discuss them. Wallets absent from a graph score zero under that graph's scores, as the plan fixed.
